:JUDGMENT:
This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 06.01.2022 wherein the petitioners have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Raghavendra due to the impact of the SCCH 15 3 MVC No.7328/2022 accident.
2.

Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of deceased Raghavendra who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 06.01.2022 due to the negligence of the rider of the respondent's motorcycle.

It is submitted that on 06.01.2022 at about 10.15 a.m.,
Raghavendra was proceeding as a pillion on Suzuki Gixxer Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KJ-2613 ridden by his friend by name Lakshmisha and when they reached near 100 feet ring road, 3rd Stage, near Inhira Canteen, PES IT college junction, Bengaluru and the motorist has ridden in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and lost control over the motorcycle and dashed against the road side median.
Due to the impact, rider and pillion rider fell down and sustained severe injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

Consequently, on 07.01.2022 a FIR No.0008/2022 was registered with the Banashankari Police station under Sec.279 and SCCH 15 4 MVC No.7328/2022 304(A) of IPC and under sec.129 and 177 of IMV Act and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and under sec.129, 177, 3(1)
Ravi Kumar K.S vs Siddappa on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104731295/
2 and 181 of IMC Act against the rider of the offending motorcycle.
The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 23 years and working as a HR Executive and was earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. at the time of accident and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.51,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
3. In pursuance of service of the notice issued, the Respondent No.1 to 3 appeared through their Counsels and filed Objections to the claim petition.

The Respondent No.1 and 2 have filed written statement submitting as follows:
SCCH 15 5 MVC No.7328/2022 It is submitted by the respondent No.1 and 2 that the alleged accident never took place due to the negligence on the part of these respondents.
The respondent No.1 is neither owner of the alleged vehicle nor driving the said vehicle.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are not necessary parties to this case.
It is submitted that the offending vehicle is insured under the respondent No.3.

It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant,
excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.

Hence, on these grounds,
Respondent No.1 and 2 have prayed to dismiss the petition against them.

4. The Respondent No.3 has filed written statement submitting as follows:
The respondent No.3 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending Suzuki Gixxer Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KJ-2613.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.3 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The rider of the said motorcycle did not have valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

Further it submitted that the deceased SCCH 15 6 MVC No.7328/2022 was travelling on the insured vehicle as a pillion rider without wearing helmet and also under influence of alcohol, hence there is a violation of provisions of Sec.129 and 185 of IMV Act.

It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioners is highly exorbitant, excessive,
arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.3 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 15.04.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Raghavendra R. S/o Ravi Kumar K.S was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on Ravi Kumar K.S vs Siddappa on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104731295/
3 06.01.2022 at about 10.15 a.m., near Indira Canteen and PES IT College, 100 feet Ring Road, BSK 3rd Stage, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Suzuki Gixer Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 02-KJ-2613?
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.7328/2022 2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal representatives of deceased Raghavendra R.?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4) What Order or Award?

6. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the Petitioner No.1 got examined as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 25 and the Respondent No.2 has got examined herself as RW.1 and respondent No.3 has examined one witness as RW.2 and relied upon Ex.R1 to 8.
7.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4 :

As per the Final Order for the following :
 SCCH 15 8 MVC No.7328/2022  REASONS 8. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the rash and negligent riding of offending Suzuki Gixxer motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KJ-2613 by its rider caused the accident (herein after referred to as offending vehicle).

9. In this regard the petitioner No.1 got examined himself as PW.1 and in his chief examination he has deposed that on 06.01.2022 at about 10.15 a.m. the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider in Suzuki Gixer motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02- 2613 which was ridden by one Lakshmisha in a rash and negligent manner on 100 feet ring road,
3rd stage, near Indira Canteen, PESIT college junction, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider lost control over the motorcycle and dashed to the road side median resulting in injuries to rider and pillion rider and pillion rider succumbed to the injuries.

4 10.

The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to SCCH 15 9 MVC No.7328/2022 describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 8 documents.

Ex.P1 - FIR registered against the rider of the offending motorcycle Lakshmisha for the offenses punishable under Sec. 279 and 304A of IPC and Sec.129 and 177 of IMV Act on the basis of the complaint given on the same day of the accident by one Rakshith, wherein it is stated by his friends that it is a self accident and Lakshmisha was the rider and Raghavendra was the pillion rider and both were succumbed to the injuries.
Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar and Ex.P4 is the spot sketch shows that the spot of the accident.

It is mentioned in FIR as well as spot sketch,
both rider and pillion rider had consumed alcohol and without wearing helmet were proceeding from Halasuru road to KEB junction ridden in a rash and negligent manner and lost control and both sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
The spot of the accident also shows that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.

In addition Ex.P8 - charge sheet is filed against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 304A of IPC SCCH 15 10 MVC No.7328/2022 and under Sec.129, 177, 3(1) and 181 of IMV Act.
It is submitted in the charge sheet that the rider of the motorcycle Lakshmisha did not have any valid DL and both were drunk as per FSL report.

The rider of the vehicle had 16.09 mg /100ml percentage alcohol and deceased pillion rider had percentage of 61.86 mg / 100 ml alcohol and hence it is clear that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as, the manner of the accident is concerned it is admitted that PW.1 is not an eye witness and not having personal knowledge about the accident and they went to AV hospital and NIMHANS,
wherein doctor reported him brought dead.
It is an admitted fact that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.
The fact that the rider of the offending motorcycle has already been charge sheeted itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.

In view of the said discussions, it is satisfactorily established that on account of rashness and negligence of rider of motorcycle instant accident has SCCH 15 11 MVC No.7328/2022 occurred resulting in the death of pillion rider.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioners and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2:
It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the, father, mother and sister of the deceased Raghavendra.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P9 to 12 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.1 to 3 and the deceased.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

13. The Petitioner No.1 is the father, Petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased, being the legal representatives of deceased Raghavendra have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Raghavendra and also they have proved that the death of the Raghavendra has been caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle, they are entitled for the compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.3:

Computation of compensation under the SCCH 15 12 MVC No.7328/2022 various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 23 years.
Ex.P-12 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the birth year of the deceased is 1996.
The alleged accident has taken place on 06.01.2022.
Hence, by considering Ex.P12, the age of the deceased is taken as 26 years.
15. Income and avocation:

As far as the income of the deceased is concerned the petitioners have deposed that the deceased Raghavendra was working in M/s Bridgelabz Solutions Pvt. Ltd., and having a salary of Rs.30,000/- per month.

In order to prove the income and avocation of the deceased, the petitioners have got examined PW.3 who is HR Counselor at M/s Bridgelabz Solutions Pvt. Ltd., and he has deposed that deceased Raghavendra was working as a HR Executive and was drawing a salary of Rs.30,000/- per month and in support of the same he SCCH 15 13 MVC No.7328/2022 has produced Ex.P18 - appointment letter of deceased Raghavendra, dated 01.02.2020, wherein it is stated that he was appointed as HR Executive on 01.02.2020.
Ex.P19 is the pay slip of the deceased for the month of October 2021, Ex
.P20 for the month of November, Ex
.P21 for the month of December, Ex

.P22 for the month of January 2022 and the Ex.P23 is the Form No.16 and on perusal of these documents it discloses that deceased was working as HR Executive and drawing salary of Rs.30,000/- per month.
16.

In addition the petitioners have also got examined PW.2 who is the Manager of ICICI Bank, who has produced statement of account and savings bank Ac/No 233401501387 and produced Ex.P16 - Statement of accounts.
On perusal of Ex.P16 it discloses that after deductions a salary of about Rs.29,000/- to 29,800/- has been remitted to the account of the deceased every month.

PW.2 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and 2 however except suggesting that the name of the father of the deceased is not mentioned in the statement of account nothing much is elicited to disprove the said statement of SCCH 15 14 MVC No.7328/2022 accounts.
PW.3 is cross

- examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 to 3 and it is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.3 that the appointment letter and acceptance letter is at Mumbai branch office and it is suggested that Ex.P18, 19 to 22 documents do not tally with each other.
PW.3 deposed that salary of deceased is remitted to ICICI bank account.
It is admitted that HR department can only tell about periodical increments and promotional benefits.
PW.3 has clearly deposed that deceased was appointed in the company on 01.02.2020.

Though it is suggested that Ex.P17 to 25 are created documents however the income and avocation of the deceased has been satisfactorily established in view of the evidence of PW.2 coupled with evidence of PW.3 and also the employment documents and statement of accounts produced by PW.2 and PW.3.
Hence the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.30,000/- per month for assessment of compensation.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be Rs.30,000X 12= 3,60,000/-.

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden SCCH 15 15 MVC No.7328/2022 principles in considering compensation Ravi Kumar K.S vs Siddappa on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104731295/
6 in cases of death.

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to SCCH 15 16 MVC No.7328/2022 the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier) Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward with the issue of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.

sentences.text: Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self- employed and was below the age of 40 years.
18. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his parents and sibling.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the SCCH 15 17 MVC No.7328/2022 time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma (supra), since the deceased was a bachelor, the deductions towards the personal expenses would be 1/2.
19.
In this Petition, the deceased was aged 26 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.42,000/- p.m. (Rs.30,000/- + Rs.12,000/- =
Rs.42,000/-).
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 17.

sentences.text: In Sarla Verma's case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held that, if the deceased was bachelor, half of his income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

20 . After deducting half of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.42,000/- it comes to Rs.21,000/- (42,000/- - 21,000/-) and multiplier applied is 17, (Rs.21,000/- x 12 = 2,52,000/-,
Rs.2,52,000/- x 17 = 42,84,000/-).
Thus, the SCCH 15 18 MVC No.7328/2022 Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.42,84,000/- towards loss of dependency.
21. Medical expenses: The petitioners have not produced any medical bills to show any expenses incurred in the hospital.
Hence the actual medical expenses incurred for the treatment of the deceased or any hospital charges are taken an Nil.
22. 'Loss of Estate', Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate',
Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-,
Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said SCCH 15 19 MVC No.7328/2022 case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

23. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-KJ-2613.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.

sentences.text: However respondent No3 insurance company has got examined its legal manager as RW.2.

It is submitted by RW.2 that there is a violation of policy conditions and the rider / insured rode his motorcycle under the influence of alcohol and without driving license and without wearing helmet and hence it is submitted that SCCH 15 21 MVC No.7328/2022 there is a breach of policy conditions and hence respondent No.3 is not liable to indemnify the rider of the offending motor cycle.
In this regard RW.2 has also produced copy of insurance policy Ex.R8.
RW.2 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 and 2 and confronted Ex.R3 to be the DL of the rider of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
On perusal of Ex.R3 is the RC and Ex.R4 - DL extract which shows that the rider of the motorcycle had valid DL on the date of the accident and DL is valid from 11.04.2006 to 10.04.2026.

It is specific contention taken by the respondent No.1 and 2 that only in case of alcohol percentage exceeding 30mg, it is considered as drunken driving however the rider of the motorcycle had only 16.09 mg as per Ex.R1 and hence it is submitted by respondent No.1 and 2 that insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
24.

In addition respondent No.2 has got examined herself as RW.1, wherein she has deposed that her son was registered owner of the offending motorcycle and stated that he had valid DL as on the date of accident and as per the test report the quantum of SCCH 15 22 MVC No.7328/2022 alcohol = 16.9 mg / 100 ml of blood and not more than 30mg and it is not considered intoxicating liquor.
In support of the same, RW.1 has produced Ex.R2 - Test report and Ex.R4 DL of the deceased Lakshmisha.
On perusal of the test report it discloses that the quantum of ethyl / alcohol present was 16.9 mg / 100 ml of blood.
Hence the prime question for consideration is as to whether the insurance company is liable to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle?.

In this regard counsel for respondent No.2 has relied on the decision laid down in MFA No.6618/2018, dated: 01.07.2025,
between K.P. Ramalingu Vs. M/s ICICI Lambard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., & another, wherein at para No.12 to 14 observed as follows:
" At this juncture, it is relevant to notice sec.185(a) of the act which reads as follows:
185. Driving by a drunken person or by a person under the influence of drugs. -
whoever, while driving or attempting to drive a motor vehicle.-

sentences.text: ( a) has, in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30mg per 100ml of blood detected in a test by a breath analyzer (or in any other test including a laboratory test).
Admittedly, in the present case, no test has been conducted on the driver so as to ascertain the extent of alcohol detected in his blood.

Learned counsel for the insurer places reliance on the finding of the tribunal where under, it has been held that having regard to the statement made by the driver in SCCH 15 23 MVC No.7328/2022 the criminal proceedings where he has admitted his guilt, the driver's admission of having consuming alcohol has been adequately proved.

In the present case, it is relevant to notice that the statement made by the driver in the criminal proceedings would not in any manner aid the case of the insurer for the purpose of attributing negligence since, in order to demonstrate that the driver was a drunken person, the criteria as stipulated under Sec.185(a) of the act would be required to be satisfied with.

In the present case, the said criteria not having been satisfied, the question of attributing any negligence to the owner of the vehicle by attributing a finding that the driver was Ravi Kumar K.S vs Siddappa on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104731295/
10 drunk at the time of the accident does not arise.

sentences.text: It is also relevant to note that the aspect of the driver having alleged to have been in a drunken state is the only factor for the finding of contributory negligence by the tribunal.
Hence the finding of the tribunal recording 25% of contributory negligence on the owner of the vehicle is erroneous and liable to be interfered with.

25. If the observation made in the said decision is taken into consideration then in this case admittedly claim petition is filed by the petitioners who are the legal representatives of the deceased pillion rider who was not rider of the motorcycle.

It has been clearly observed in the judgment referred to supra that it is the insurer who is liable to pay compensation even if the driver intoxicated at the time of the accident if the violation under section 185(a) of MV Act is not proved.

As per the test report it discloses that the quantum of ethyl / alcohol present was 16.9 mg / 100 ml of blood of rider of the motor cycle which is much below the limit SCCH 15 24 MVC No.7328/2022 prescribed under section 185(a) of the MV Act.
Hence though the Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However the Respondent No.3 who is the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and 2 and will have to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".

26. Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.44,65,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the SCCH 15 25 MVC No.7328/2022 following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.44,65,500/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.3 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:

5. Vide order dated 15.04.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Raghavendra R. S/o Ravi Kumar K.S was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on Ravi Kumar K.S vs Siddappa on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104731295/
3 06.01.2022 at about 10.15 a.m., near Indira Canteen and PES IT College, 100 feet Ring Road, BSK 3rd Stage, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Suzuki Gixer Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 02-KJ-2613?
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.7328/2022 2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal representatives of deceased Raghavendra R.?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The rider of the vehicle had 16.09 mg /100ml percentage alcohol and deceased pillion rider had percentage of 61.86 mg / 100 ml alcohol and hence it is clear that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
It is an admitted fact that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.
The fact that the rider of the offending motorcycle has already been charge sheeted itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of the said discussions, it is satisfactorily established that on account of rashness and negligence of rider of motorcycle instant accident has SCCH 15 11 MVC No.7328/2022 occurred resulting in the death of pillion rider.
13. The Petitioner No.1 is the father, Petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of the deceased, being the legal representatives of deceased Raghavendra have a right to apply for compensation.
As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Raghavendra and also they have proved that the death of the Raghavendra has been caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle, they are entitled for the compensation.

5 14.
The alleged accident has taken place on 06.01.2022.
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden SCCH 15 15 MVC No.7328/2022 principles in considering compensation Ravi Kumar K.S vs Siddappa on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104731295/
6 in cases of death.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self- employed and was below the age of 40 years.
18. At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his parents and sibling.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the SCCH 15 17 MVC No.7328/2022 time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.
In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

9
It is submitted by RW.2 that there is a violation of policy conditions and the rider / insured rode his motorcycle under the influence of alcohol and without driving license and without wearing helmet and hence it is submitted that SCCH 15 21 MVC No.7328/2022 there is a breach of policy conditions and hence respondent No.3 is not liable to indemnify the rider of the offending motor cycle.
In the present case, it is relevant to notice that the statement made by the driver in the criminal proceedings would not in any manner aid the case of the insurer for the purpose of attributing negligence since, in order to demonstrate that the driver was a drunken person, the criteria as stipulated under Sec.185(a) of the act would be required to be satisfied with.
In the present case, the said criteria not having been satisfied, the question of attributing any negligence to the owner of the vehicle by attributing a finding that the driver was Ravi Kumar K.S vs Siddappa on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104731295/
10 drunk at the time of the accident does not arise.
It is also relevant to note that the aspect of the driver having alleged to have been in a drunken state is the only factor for the finding of contributory negligence by the tribunal.
Hence the finding of the tribunal recording 25% of contributory negligence on the owner of the vehicle is erroneous and liable to be interfered with.
Hence though the Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
